evidence.claim: Current v0.36 defines startup-owner diagnostics, separate control/recovery states, verified archive reuse, scoped install verification and representative full-history measurement without changing file authority or unknown-write rules.
CLI reports controlled service build metadata and recovery diagnostics, sends ordinary RPC directly and retains existing request/outcome semantics.

Loopback service preserves authenticated admission and recovery boundaries; browser login reports missing sessions, expired codes and invalid/used codes, and checking a valid session does not rotate or extend it.

Runtime shares verified worktree archives across background recovery and ordinary resources, serializes subscription resumption with registry mutations, exposes recovery progress and blocks GC apply during recovery.
WorkspaceRegistry preserves existing identities and files; unregistered Git worktrees return ask-user, an actual path/impact question, and fallback only after decline or cancellation.
LikeC4 and evidence/aliases form one model snapshot, retaining evidence identities and document Git diagnostics without rewriting authored status.

TaskService restores all committed task contracts incrementally and verifies known-task references without copying unrelated payloads; task-read projection uses commit headers while historical bytes and retention stay unchanged.
Actual skill files and references are scanned, versioned and captured as editable file content.

File-authoritative Archive derives bounded type/task queries, copies only matching records or reference/header data, yields during large journal parsing and deduplicates references within a recovery pass without a lifetime trust cache.
SearchIndex sends typed operations to a separate SQLite worker and supports derived projection rebuilding.
Source scanning captures actual Git/file scope and fingerprints without interpreting business semantics.

FreshnessManager observes declared and boundary-checked real reference paths before exclusions, maps directory notifications to affected evidence files, rejects stale epochs, and preserves unrelated pending scope during verification.
ObservationManager restores explicit log bindings and checkpoint/events from the file archive.
Ordinary legacy discovery uses the owning verified archive and ordered commit metadata; explicit migration/requested legacy bytes and conservative GC retain existing checks and protected content.
Formal Web preserves task targets and archived projections; interrupted sign-in has an explicit retry state, and fresh login fragments arriving in the same document reload authentication.

Web confirms browser cookies before clearing successful sign-in credentials, retains the original URL on transient failures, clears explicitly rejected credentials with targets preserved, and keeps actual HTTP 401 reasons.
Runtime entry prioritizes onboarding over generic failure fallback, asks before first setup even with old CLI fields, and retains existing context, document and output-card duties.
Bundled methods are self-contained within each selected folder; editable user files and archived bytes retain their existing boundaries.
Formal CLI builds stamp provenance and ship explicit skill-installation and runtime-verification tools; prototype scripts remain separate.
Frozen v0.16 prototype and MGRP examples remain historical/reference material separate from the formal implementation.
Text authority defines document identity, current reference lifecycle and read-only Git diagnostics; document bodies still require explicit reading.

Controller distinguishes live startup ownership from stopped/authenticated endpoints, joins bounded startup without spawning a competitor, sanitizes optional build metadata and preserves pre-execution-only RPC retries.
Formal Web documentation describes sign-in recovery, precise credential cleanup, isolated program/browser regression commands and existing projection gates without claiming unrun platforms.
Context layout keeps hit paths, explicit returned parent-body leaves and unmatched overflows without duplicating entity counts or changing the complete directory.
Skill layout preserves saved selection identities and groups, aggregates unselected catalog members and folders, and omits unselected file nodes.
Standalone context and skill directories provide scoped search, hit filtering and 50-row paging with explicit inspection and candidate actions.
Batch read-only Git classification distinguishes tracked, untracked, ignored and unknown local document evidence without staging or changing source exclusions.

Explicit references include .harness and safe in-worktree link targets without expanding source scans; scoped verification handles real paths and native casing while preserving unrelated pending work and history.

Storage keeps journal authority, bounded derived record queries and pass-local reference verification, separates build provenance from sourceVersion and protects historical bytes during install or rollback.
Default methods link only to their own archived attachments; user related candidates remain optional and historical bytes remain immutable.
Runtime reference explains UTF-8 request construction, PowerShell pipeline loss, immutable damaged history and scoped phase maintenance.
Static help exposes the build source without starting the service and retains command/schema discovery and version semantics.
A conservative display-only predicate marks suspected damaged reasons without changing archived input.
Skill details show a suspected encoding warning and expose the exact saved reason on demand.
Isolated browser checks exercise Unicode, damaged and operator reasons, self-contained review bytes, and unchanged saved plans/batches.

Installer regression covers canonical attachment paths, linked skill roots, byte-preserving backups and direct execution through a package directory alias with JSON, reinstallation and invalid-argument checks.
Native linked-reference regressions check repaired physical/alternative scopes and preserve a sibling document pending after partial verification.
Current status records the first-use consent-routing correction, 34 passing Windows checks, updated host skill files, unchanged installed CLI/service and pending real-host consent verification.

The explicit runtime-skill installer uses Node main-module identity so aliased entry paths execute its JSON CLI; imports do not perform installation. Existing backup and destination-link checks remain.

A fresh installed package through a Unicode directory alias exercises runtime fingerprint/service identity, archived handoff comparison and changed-baseline rejection, plus existing skill/task/login/offline checks.
Isolated HTTP/CLI regressions cover joining an existing startup owner, sanitized metadata and prior classified health, admission, endpoint rotation, death recovery and lost committed responses.
Retained prototype model watching reconciles content hashes after missed native notifications, skips unchanged parsing, and cancels reconciliation when closed.
Real-file prototype regressions retain the native watcher deadline and inject lost notifications to verify equal-length content edits update the parsed model and persisted valid revision.

Explicit installer verification checks package/runtime provenance, the actual resident build and RPC, optionally compares a saved handoff, and reports completed phases without automatically replaying failed business requests.
CLI build stamping records actual Git provenance or unknown, dependency-lock bytes and compiled runtime fingerprint without exposing machine paths or credentials.
Package helpers expose a restricted build projection and fingerprint packaged runtime files; missing provenance remains unknown.
The platform installation flows preserve an old package, verify the expected clean source and running build, and describe explicit saved-handoff checks and data-preserving rollback.
Update guidance saves an actual UTF-8 handoff before stopping the old service, compares it after update and distinguishes copied files, host loading and checked versus unrequested recovery.
Isolated real-server tests block archive recovery while checking control readiness/RPC and GC exclusion, and count shared-content reads across startup and first worktree access.

A separate synthetic two-worktree benchmark seeds full TaskService histories and measures fresh-process control readiness, total first handoff, warm RPC and peak RSS while checking authoritative journal hashes.
Archive regressions exercise single-pass shared-reference validation, later corruption, filtered immutable record/reference queries and invocation-boundary iteration alongside durability checks.
The actual CLI reports a live unpublished startup owner as unavailable, rejects false stop success, and leaves the lock and owner intact.
Known-ID handoff returns the original packet without copying unrelated committed history; existing source/CAS, retention, historical and corrupt-archive checks remain.

TC17/22/23/26 retain recovery, installation and archive boundaries; TC23 additionally checks interrupted authentication and confirmation, cookie failures, fresh-fragment recovery, unchanged cookie expiry and task records.
Architecture separates preflight/control availability from background recovery while retaining singleton ownership, full target verification, explicit subscriptions and safe shutdown.
Protocol preserves existing command semantics and adds explicit ask-user, question and fallbackWhen fields to noninteractive first-use guidance.
FR12/14 distinguish control, recovery and install-check state and require independent representative accumulated-history measurements.
The specification entry points at current baseline v0.36 and its scoped installation/recovery refinements without inheriting old platform verification.

Performance documentation records a same-history baseline/candidate comparison and a separately sampled candidate steady-read supplement with exact recovery-wait, runtime fingerprint, integrity checks and platform/synthetic limitations; prior small-record results remain independently scoped.
Agent maintenance follows baseline v0.36, preserves startup ownership and separates copied files, running build and applicable archived handoff verification.
The existing synthetic fixture generator is reusable by the full-history benchmark; its prior small-record/core/CLI methodology remains separately scoped.
Client regressions check interrupted and malformed sign-in, delayed cookie confirmation, rejected credentials, missing cookies, cleaned URLs, exact targets and legacy HTTP 401 responses.
An isolated real HTTP service distinguishes missing, invalid/used and expired login codes with a test clock, while valid cookies, fixed expiry and origin rejection remain enforced.

The browser regression injects interrupted first and confirmation requests plus missing cookies, exercises button and same-document fresh-link recovery, and checks credential cleanup, exact target, unchanged session expiry and task archive.
Web authentication recovery preserves retry credentials only on transient failures, confirms browser sessions, handles fresh fragments and keeps precise rejection and target boundaries.
First-use routing requires an agent question before setup, reuses authorization, and limits fallback to decline/cancel, including older CLI guidance.
Usage explains TARGET_REQUIRED onboarding as pending user confirmation, with agent UI or conversational questioning and no automatic initialization.
Isolated CLI checks require explicit ask-user and conditional fallback for initialization and registration, preserve worktree bytes before consent and reject unrelated target onboarding.
